claim: [6iii] We’re furnishing the house in a modern style / the Italian fashion “illustrates the case where there is no adverb at all derived from the adjective (∗modernly, ∗Italianly)”.
evidence_summary: Wiktionary has modernly, ‘in a modern manner or style’, quoting Anthony Byars, Texas, in Fact (2004): The living room was huge and modernly furnished. That is the manner sense, with the verb of [6iii]. The book itself hasn’t been seen. Wiktionary also lists Italianly, ‘in an Italian manner’, with no quotation.
finding: A lead, not yet a finding. If edited prose attests manner modernly, the claim needs qualifying: the paragraph speaks of “natural counterparts”, so the point may be that the adverb is unavailable in ordinary use, but the ∗ says more than that.

evidence.passage: §2.1, p. 671. “there is no adverb at all derived from the adjective (∗modernly, ∗Italianly)”.
evidence.example: Wiktionary entry for modernly, read as wikitext.
evidence.establishes: A lead only. Merriam-Webster returned HTTP 403 to the audit tools.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.

evidence.source: Wiktionary, “modernly” (revision 93708141), quoting Anthony Byars, Texas, in Fact (2004).
evidence.example: “The living room was huge and modernly furnished.”
evidence.establishes: A quoted use of manner modernly with furnish, at second hand. The book hasn’t been checked.
